title: Vegan Banana Bread Cupcakes
shortDescription: Soft banana cupcakes with a cinnamon cream swirl, ready in 25 minutes prep and 18 minutes bake.
description: These cupcakes taste like banana bread but come together faster and bake evenly in a muffin tin. Ripe bananas add natural sweetness, so we use less sugar than a typical vegan cupcake recipe. I tested this batch with bananas so spotty they were almost black, and that is exactly what you want. The riper the banana, the deeper the flavor and the moister the crumb The frosting is a simple vegan buttercream swirled with cinnamon, so every bite tastes like a warm slice of banana bread with extra frosting on top. No eggs, no dairy, no fuss. This recipe works well for breakfast-style cupcakes or a cozy fall dessert table.
ingredients: 1 tsp ground cinnamon, plus 1/2 tsp for frosting
1/3 cup neutral oil, such as canola or melted coconut oil
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F and line a muffin tin with 12 cupcake liners.
In a medium bowl, whisk flour, baking soda, salt, and 1 tsp cinnamon.
In a large bowl, mash bananas until mostly smooth with a few small lumps.
Whisk sugar, oil, almond milk, vanilla, and vinegar into the mashed bananas.
Fold the dry ingredients into the wet ingredients until just combined. Do not overmix.
Divide batter evenly among the liners, filling each about two thirds full.
Bake 16 to 18 minutes, until a toothpick comes out clean.
Cool cupcakes in the tin for 5 minutes, then move to a wire rack to cool fully.
Beat vegan butter until smooth, then add powdered sugar and 1/2 tsp cinnamon.
Beat frosting on high for 2 minutes until light and fluffy, then pipe onto cooled cupcakes.
tips: Use bananas with lots of brown spots. They mash easier and taste sweeter.
Do not overmix the batter, or the cupcakes will turn dense instead of soft.
If your frosting feels too soft, chill it for 15 minutes before piping.
Add a small pinch of nutmeg to the frosting for a deeper spice flavor.

faq.question: Can I use frozen bananas for this recipe?
faq.answer: Yes. Thaw them fully first and drain any extra liquid before mashing, so the batter does not turn watery.

faq.question: Why did my cupcakes turn out dense?
faq.answer: This usually means the batter was overmixed. Stir just until the flour disappears, then stop.

faq.question: Can I add walnuts or chocolate chips?
faq.answer: Yes. Fold in 1/2 cup chopped walnuts or vegan chocolate chips right before dividing the batter into liners.

faq.question: How do I store these cupcakes?
faq.answer: Store frosted cupcakes in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 4 days. Bring to room temperature before serving.

conclusion: These banana bread cupcakes bring cozy flavor with simple, honest ingredients. Frost them high with cinnamon cream and share them with anyone, vegan or not.
